newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse sets up new IPO allocation scheme.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse sets up new IPO allocation scheme.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Thursday its board had approved a new distribution scheme for initial public offerings (IPO).
In the past, broker-members were alloted 50 percent of an IPO through the bourse which then equally distributed among them.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) had called for scrapping of the scheme saying that brokerage firms, especially the inactive ones, just sat on the shares and bought them on their own account if they acquired a premium in the grey market.
If the issues failed, the brokers just returned them to the underwriters defeating the purpose it was given to the brokers, which was that they should distribute it to small investors.
The SEC's suggestion to abolish the scheme evoked fierce opposition from brokers.

PSE president Vitaliano Nanagas said a new scheme has been set up where brokers will have to inform underwriters on the third day of the offering on whether they will subscribe and how much shares they will buy. The underwriters will then distribute the shares according to the demand.
"The PSE will undertake and guarantee that its brokers will exert their best efforts to distribute these IPO shares as widely as possible," Nanagas said.
SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay, in the same press conference, said the regulatory authority had decided to give a conditional self-regulating organisation (SRO) status to the bourse.
"There has been substantive compliance with our requirements," Yasay said.

The conditional SRO status will be given on November 15. The bourse has until February next year to come up with a detailed regulatory plan on how they will enforce the allocation and auditing programmes.
Nanagas said the bourse had suspended the small investors' programme (SIP) which was aimed at distributing the initial public offering (IPO) to a larger share of investors.

Under the SIP, 10 percent of any public offering worth more than one billion pesos will be distributed to retail investors. Small investors were those who were allowed to buy up to 10,000 pesos worth of shares from a central distribution centre.

"The suspension of the SIP does not mean that we will halt our efforts to reach out to the small investor. In fact, PSE ... will be working towards a better system, a much improved system than the SIP," PSE president Vitaliano Nanagas said in a statement.
He said the present set-up does not guarantee prospective investors full information about the company.
